title: MOESI cache coherence protocol
summary: MOESI extends MESI with an Owned (O) state: Modified (M), Owned (O), Exclusive (E), Shared (S), Invalid (I). Owned state: line is dirty and shared (this cache is responsible for writing back; others have read-only copies). Reduces write-backs compared to MESI (which requires M->I transition on snoop write, forcing a write-back).

structure.meaning: Dirty and exclusive. Write back on eviction.
Dirty and shared. This cache owns the line (responsible for write-back). Others have read-only (S) copies.
When another cache reads a Modified line, it transitions to Owned (instead of Shared in MESI), keeping the dirty data in this cache.
On a snoop write, Owned transitions to Invalid (write back first).

notes: MOESI reduces memory traffic by keeping dirty data in cache longer.
Used by AMD (Opteron) and some ARM implementations.
MESIF (Intel) uses Forward instead of Owned for efficient sharing.
